liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Sugaree** (2 reviews): Show-opening Sugaree runs over thirteen minutes and is described as thick and hot; Reviewer singles out Sugaree as a great performance [14][22]
- **Loser** (2 reviews): Loser has an Old West feel with a soaring Garcia lead; Reviewer singles out Loser as a great performance [18][22]
- **New Minglewood Blues** (1 review): Reviewer says Minglewood and Beat It On Down The Line were played with gusto [18]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Reviewer singles out the Peggy-O as touching and beautiful, one of their favorites of the show [12]
- **Beat It On Down The Line** (1 review): Reviewer calls Beat It On Down The Line a true smoker [17]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Reviewer thinks this Looks Like Rain may be the best ever version [20]
- **Big River** (1 review): Reviewer likes the nice ride of Big River, credited to Billy [17]
- **Deal** (1 review): First-set closing Deal is praised as dominant, with strong lead guitar [14]

## Setlist highlights

- **Beat It On Down The Line**: cut on the recording [24]
- **Sunrise**: cut on the recording [24]
- **Encore Crowd Call**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1978-05-06.aud.glassberg.motb.82963.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 20 songs; 179 min; rated 4.8/5 by 5 [1]
- **gd78-05-06.rolfe.vernon.6711.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 176 min; rated 4.09/5 by 11 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says this copy sounds better than the other audience copy on offer; Reviewer hears unusual clarity and quickness in this audience recording for May 1978; Recording is not muffled; Jerry's voice leaps out immediately and crowd sounds come at the right places [14][15][16]
- **gd78-05-06.glassberg.vernon.18657.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 170 min; rated 3.6/5 by 5 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience recording sounds bad: Jerry's voice and occasional loud guitar are heard, while crowd clapping dominates and grates [13]
- **gd1978-05-06.171364.sony.ecm99a.rolfe.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 175 min [4]
- **gd78-05-06.sbd-aud.cotsman.13726.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 158 min; rated 4.27/5 by 22 [6]. Said about its sound: Soundboard portion, first set only, sounds warm and full, typical of late 70s; the rest is audience recording [22]
- **gd1978-05-06.set2.aud.unknown.GEMS.92356.flac16**: audience recording; 8 songs; 77 min; rated 3.33/5 by 3 [10]. Said about its sound: Uploader thinks it sounds closer to the stage than the Glassberg version, with strong crowd energy [10]

## Around the show

- Reviewer is surprised the concert took place in a gym and notes a very enthusiastic audience [12]
- Reviewer notes Donna was in tune and wishes Phil's volume were higher in the mix [17]
- Reviewer attended the show and remembers being floored; it took years to find a tape [20]
- Reviewer says the band's spring 78 run moved from April to May much as 1977 did [15]
- Reviewer says the spring 78 tour was hit and miss with stale repertoire, but this show was a hit [18]
- Reviewer ranks the show alongside most 1977 shows [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1978-05-06.aud.glassberg.motb.82963.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by A. Egert and D. McCabe; source: FOB Audience Recording (25th Row DFC ) Nakamichi CM300's > Sony 1535D (Dolby B on) > MAC [1]. Also: Beat It On Down The Line and It Must Have Been The Roses were processed with Izotope Ozone, with curve compensating for no Dolby B [1]
- **gd78-05-06.rolfe.vernon.6711.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Steve Rolfe; source: Audience Recording [2]. Also: Recorded by Steve Rolfe on Sony ECM-99A mics to Sony TC-152 cassette, then to DAT, with no processing; DAT to shn transfer was done by Dale Shepherd [2]
- **gd78-05-06.glassberg.vernon.18657.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by John Steinthal; source: Audience Recording: NAK CM700, Sony 158SD [3]
- **gd1978-05-06.171364.sony.ecm99a.rolfe.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Steve Rolfe; transferred by Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Steve Rolfe's Master Audience Cassettes; Sony ECM-99A mics > Sony TC-152SD (Maxell UD-C90) [4]. Also: A 13-second patch in Drums comes from a three-mic blend source [4]
- **gd78-05-06.sbd-aud.cotsman.13726.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard and Audience Composite [6]
- **gd1978-05-06.set2.aud.unknown.GEMS.92356.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Jamie Waddell; source: FOB, unknown mics [10]. Also: Second-set audience tape is about second-generation cassette, from friend of the tapers, reportedly tenth row center [10]

## Art and photos

- Poster by www.photog.com: [Grateful Dead UVM Patrick Gymnasium 6 May 1978 James R Anderson Photography](https://www.photog.com/gdead/70s/78/05-06/index.html) [25]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Patrick Gym - May 6, 1978](https://www.dead.net/show/may-6-1978) [26]
